title: Prepaid commitment rollovers, negative-balance caps, and security billing disclosures
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers have raised multiple related edge cases during contract negotiations and security questionnaire reviews: (1) how prepaid commitments roll over (or do not) when a customer downgrades mid-cycle; (2) whether automatic negative balances (overages exceeding credits) should be capped or converted to invoices immediately; (3) operational rules for partial customer-initiated refunds on committed seats/credits; and (4) what billing controls and disclosures must be included in our public security questionnaire and contract templates to satisfy procurement teams.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document a deterministic rollover policy for prepaid commitments (explicit behavior when customer downgrades, upgrades, or pauses service mid-cycle)
Implement rule for negative-balance overages: capped hold amount vs immediate billing, with feature-flagged implementation for canary customers
Support partial refunds for prepaid credits with audit trail: request -> verify -> refund -> audit entry -> accounting reconciliation link
Update security questionnaire / SOC/GDPR billing disclosure language to reflect the above mechanics and controls (include retention and data-handling statements relevant to billing logs)
Provide test harness and sample invoices for 5 canonical scenarios (upgrade mid-cycle, downgrade mid-cycle, pause then resume, large overage with cap, customer refund request)
QA: regression tests added to billing ledger and invoice generation code paths; integration test with metering pipeline validates sequence numbers and idempotency
updates: 2025-02-20: Ticket created after onboarding call with large enterprise prospect; prospect flagged rollover ambiguity in SOW and asked for explicit language in security questionnaire.

2025-02-24: Cross-functional sync with Accounting (J. Rivera) and Legal (M. Chen) — Accounting prefers immediate invoice for negative balances; Legal requests a capped 'grace overage' option for enterprise negotiability.

2025-02-27: Experiment design drafted: two options (A: capped negative balance with invoice threshold; B: immediate invoice with automatic credit application). Decided to run canary on 3 enterprise customers for 6 weeks under feature flag.

2025-03-01: Engineering spike (ENG-5489) completed to surface ledger-level hooks for partial refund workflow; identified required event fields (original_purchase_id, refund_reason_code, processed_by).

2025-03-04: PRD updated with sample wording for security questionnaire and contract SOW clause. Requesting design review and Legal sign-off. Assigned implementation to next billing sprint after canary gating plan finalized.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: customer UX clarity vs accounting simplicity. Accounting prefers immediate invoice recognition; sales prefers rollover and caps to simplify negotiations.
Proposed rollout: feature-flagged cap model (option A) exposed to enterprise toggles in Console for dedicated/private customers; hosted customers default to immediate invoice until product is stable.
Follow-ups: update contract template clause, add SSO audit trail for refund workflows, add telemetry events for every state transition in billing state machine.
